limits: 'own scope' is the union of the names the enclosing constructs bind (comprehension generator targets and lambda parameters, all constructs on the chain); a site whose construct is the second one of a nested pair is not told apart from the first

a name can be bound in the own scope and still hold an outer row (the caller can pass the row in, or the generator can iterate over rows); the published class says where the name is bound, not what object it carries at run time

classic loops over a row set are module-body sites with a for-guard (E649's loop bucket), not comprehension sites, so the same per-item read pattern is priced in another bucket and is not part of these 383

a subscript addressed through a call or an attribute chain publishes the leftmost name (E633's own rule) or no base at all; no base means the scope cannot be read off the construct and the site is published as unresolved_base, not guessed

the key is a literal string here; a computed key (a variable, a join, an f-string) has no literal key and therefore never matches a counted key in this face (E645 and E651 price computed keys in their own arms)
the exclusion list drops only this study's own files, so the sibling studies' scripts stay inside the population and the site totals are slightly larger than E643's own
files over 1MB are skipped rather than parsed (E391's cap) and are counted apart
